item.description: Shep’s Paradise and the Survival of Clarissa Street (1967) In 1967, Ruther “Shep” Sheppard purchased a bar at 293 Clarissa Street. item.title: Urban Renewal and the Dismantling of Clarissa Street (Late 1960s–Early 1970s)
item.description: By the late 1960s and early 1970s, federal urban renewal programs reshaped Rochester’s landscape. Entire sections of the Clarissa Street neighborhood were demolished. Urban renewal was often marketed as modernization. In practice, it frequently meant displacement. Black families who had built homes and businesses over generations were uprooted.
